record.original_question: Study the complexity function of polygonal symplectic billiards, where the complexity p(n) counts the number of length-n subwords arising from symbolic codings of billiard trajectories by polygon sides.

evidence.quote: Complexity of polygonal symplectic billiards.Symplectic billiards were introduced in [10]; the polygonal ones were studied in [4, 8]. Label the sides of a polygon by some symbols and assign to a billiard trajectory its symbolic code, the corresponding bi-infinite word in these symbols. The set of all trajectories yields a collection of such words. The complexity functionp(n)is the number of different subwords of lengthnin this collection. For the conventional polygonal billiards, it is known that the complexity function is sub- exponential (the literature on this subject is huge, starting with [82]), and it has polynomial, actually cubic, growth for rational billiards (whose angles are rational multiples ofπ). For polygonal outer billiards, the growth of the complexity function is polynomial, see [67]. Problem:study the complexity of polygonal symplectic billiards.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup (symplectic billiards in a convex polygon). Let P ⊂ R² be a convex polygon with sides s_1, …, s_k (labeled by symbols from an alphabet A = {1, …, k}). The symplectic billiard map T acts on ordered pairs of boundary points (x, y) ∈ ∂P × ∂P (with x ≠ y) by the following rule: T(x, y) = (y, z), where z ∈ ∂P is uniquely determined by the condition that the chord xz is parallel to the tangent line to ∂P at y. (At a vertex of P, "tangent direction" is interpreted via the supporting lines, and the map is defined on the full-measure set where this rule is unambiguous.)

Symbolic coding. Given a bi-infinite orbit (…, x_{-1}, x_0, x_1, …) of T whose points lie in the interiors of sides, assign to it the bi-infinite word w ∈ A^Z whose n-th letter is the index of the side containing x_n. Let L ⊂ A^Z denote the language consisting of all finite words that occur as factors (subwords) of the codings of all such orbits, as P is fixed.

Complexity function. For each integer n ≥ 1, define
   p(n) = #{ u ∈ A^n : u is a factor of some w ∈ L }.

Problem. Determine the asymptotic behavior of the complexity function p(n) of polygonal symplectic billiards. In particular:
(a) Establish general upper and lower bounds on p(n) valid for all convex polygons P (e.g., is p(n) sub-exponential?).
(b) For "rational" polygons (those whose angles are rational multiples of π, or any natural analogue suited to the symplectic setting), determine the precise polynomial growth rate of p(n).
(c) Identify classes of polygons (such as affine-regular polygons or trapezoids, where every orbit is periodic) for which p(n) is bounded, and more generally classify possible growth rates of p(n) in terms of geometric properties of P.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in a recent open-problems collection on billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry. While complexity functions for conventional polygonal billiards (sub-exponential in general, cubic for rational/tiling cases) and for polygonal outer billiards (polynomial) are well studied, the analogous study for polygonal symplectic billiards remains open. Partial information is available: in special polygons (e.g., affine-regular polygons, trapezoids) every symplectic billiard orbit is periodic, so p(n) is bounded; the general asymptotics are not established.

status_evidence.title: Polygonal symplectic billiards
status_evidence.snippet: In affine-regular polygons and trapezoids, all orbits are periodic with explicitly described periods.
status_evidence.claim: For some polygons all orbits are periodic, so p(n) is bounded; general behavior is not known.

status_evidence.title: Complexity and growth for polygonal billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Cubic complexity bounds for rational polygonal (Birkhoff) billiards.
status_evidence.claim: Analogous classical results exist only for ordinary polygonal billiards, not symplectic ones.

status_evidence.title: On the complexity of polygonal billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on complexity for ordinary polygonal billiards.
status_evidence.claim: Recent activity continues on classical billiards; symplectic case still open.
